headline: Shift Grid Costs to Large Users
short_summary: This bill aims to shift certain electricity costs, including capacity market costs and new distribution infrastructure, from residential ratepayers to large energy users like data centers, potentially saving residential customers money.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer advocates, environmental groups, some lawmakers.
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users, Dominion Energy (initially opposed amendments).
news_headline: Governor amends bills that shift costs onto data centers. Critics say her tweaks weaken them.
news_summary: Governor Spanberger signed legislation, including HB 1393, that directs regulators to assign electricity costs to data centers, aiming to save residential customers money. However, her amendments removed a provision that would have directly shifted capacity market costs, instead giving the State Corporation Commission authority to determine fair cost allocation.

headline: Mandate Data Center Water Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires water users supplying data centers to report monthly or quarterly water consumption, including reclaimed water, to the State Water Control Board for transparency and planning.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities concerned about water resources, transparency advocates.
opponents: Data center industry (due to increased reporting burden).
news_headline: Four data center bills await governor's signature as Southwest Virginia projects spark debate
news_summary: SB 553, which increases reporting requirements for data center water usage, was among several bills on the governor's desk aimed at regulating data centers. Supporters emphasize the need for transparency on water use, especially given concerns about local water impacts from proposed data center projects.

headline: Regulate Data Center Siting & Noise
short_summary: This bill requires local governments to review potential impacts, including noise studies and other environmental effects, before approving new data centers, especially those using 100 megawatts or more.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental groups, local planning organizations.
opponents: Data center industry, developers, chambers of commerce (concerned about delays and costs).
news_headline: What does Data center site assessment and sound profile for high energy use facilities (HB153) do?
news_summary: HB 153 requires Virginia local governments to review potential impacts, including noise and effects on nearby homes and schools, before approving new data centers of 100 megawatts or more. It also allows localities to request reviews on water, farmland, parks, historic sites, and forests to ensure informed decisions.
